evals.prompt: Run a full sweep while another agent is implementing tasks in the same repo.
evals.expected_output: A parallel-safe audit workflow that never edits source files, stages findings, and drains them into TASKS.md at the end.
expectations: States that sweep is read-only for source files and safe to run alongside an implementation worker
Uses TASKS-AUDIT.md as a per-session staging buffer, not a persistent queue
Stages only TASKS.md and TASKS-AUDIT.md and never uses git add .
Drains every finding into TASKS.md P3 in one atomic session-end commit

evals.prompt: The queue already has 20 unclaimed P0-P2 tasks. Sweep the repo for more work.
evals.expected_output: A deliver-mode sweep that throttles proactive findings because the actionable queue is already full.
expectations: Runs the queue-pressure check before launching tier subagents
Selects DELIVER mode when P0-P2 unclaimed tasks exceed the threshold
Runs only the verify gate and existing-queue rot check instead of all audit tiers
Allows only clearly surfaced P0 findings from the verify gate rather than generating broad net-new audit work

evals.prompt: Sweep this CLI repo for stability, test depth, docs, dependencies, DX, and vision gaps.
evals.expected_output: A multi-tier sweep plan that uses git history to focus read-only subagents and avoids duplicate task creation.
expectations: Detects project type and verification commands before audit tiers run
Runs git-diagnose-codebase or equivalent git-log commands to prioritize high-risk files
Launches or conceptually separates tier-specific read-only audits for stability, tests, docs, code health, dependencies, DX, and vision
Reads existing TASKS.md first and suppresses duplicate findings

evals.prompt: Run a full codebase sweep to find all no-brainer improvements and stage them for implementation.
evals.expected_output: A TASKS-AUDIT.md file with findings from all 8 audit tiers (verify gate, stability, testing, docs, code health, dependencies, DX/UX, vision alignment), deduplicated and prioritized into P0/P1/P2/P3 tasks.
expectations: Detects project type (TypeScript, Python, Rust, etc.) and identifies appropriate verify commands (tsc, eslint, pytest, cargo test, etc.)
Runs git-diagnose-codebase to identify high-churn files and bug clusters, biasing subsequent tiers toward highest-risk code
Checks queue pressure (P0-P2 unclaimed task count) and decides between DELIVER mode (Tier 1 only) vs ADD mode (all 8 tiers)
Executes Tier 1 (verify gate) and reports all compiler errors, lint violations, test failures, and security vulnerabilities as P0 findings
Executes Tier 2 (stability) and identifies silent error swallowing, missing timeouts, unhandled promise rejections, and resource leaks
Executes Tier 3 (test depth) and flags source files with no tests, low assertion density, and missing edge case coverage

evals.prompt: Our codebase has accumulated technical debt. Run a sweep focused on code health and dependencies to find refactoring opportunities.
evals.expected_output: A TASKS-AUDIT.md with findings from Tier 5 (code health) and Tier 6 (dependencies) including large files, dead code, duplicate patterns, and outdated dependencies.
expectations: Identifies source files over 300 lines as candidates for splitting, with specific line ranges and suggested module boundaries
Finds functions with deep nesting (>4 levels) or high cyclomatic complexity (>10 branches) using static analysis
Detects duplicate code patterns across files using similarity heuristics, grouping similar blocks together
Identifies dead code: exported functions never imported, unused variables, unreachable branches
Runs npm outdated / cargo outdated / pip list --outdated and reports major version updates separately from minor/patch
Finds unused dependencies in package.json/Cargo.toml/pyproject.toml that are never imported

evals.prompt: I want to understand what's broken and what's missing in our project before I start implementing. Run a sweep with focus on vision alignment.
evals.expected_output: A TASKS-AUDIT.md with findings from Tier 8 (vision alignment) showing user story implementation status, README accuracy, and competitive gaps.
expectations: Reads docs/user-stories.md (or equivalent) and checks each story against the codebase for implementation status (implemented / partial / missing)
Produces a coverage table mapping each user story to code evidence or noting it as aspirational
Verifies README feature claims against actual exports, commands, and working code
Checks VISION.md goals for corresponding code or tasks, flagging aspirational features with no implementation
Reads docs/COMPETITION.md (if present) and identifies competitor features that would be easy wins
Reviews API surface (CLI commands, exported functions, REST endpoints) for coherence and overlaps
